chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about the man who takes a security deposit for a mortgage of one hundred Dirhams and it is equated to three hundred Dirhams, so it is destroyed. Is it upon the man that he returns to his companion two hundred Dirhams? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, because he took a deposit wherein was excess, and wasted it.' I said, 'Supposing half the deposit was destroyed?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It would be upon the reckoning of that.' I said, 'So they would both be returning the excess?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pledged item is destroyed while in the creditor's possession?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *ghurm bi al-ghurm* (liability corresponds to benefit) in Islamic finance, establishing that the creditor bears the risk of loss for the collateral's value exceeding the debt. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness, ensuring the creditor does not unjustly retain the 'excess' value (*fadl*) of the pledged item if it perishes while in their custody. This ruling serves as a foundational precedent for modern Islamic banking contracts involving collateral and risk allocation.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, from Hammad Bin Usman, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Ibrahim<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) about the man who took a security deposit for a mortgage of one hundred Dirhams and it was equated to three hundred Dirham. So it was destroyed. Is it upon the man that he returns two hundred Dirhams to his companion?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, because he took the deposit wherein was excess, and wasted it’. I said, ‘Supposing half deposit was destroyed?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It would be upon the reckoning of that’. I said, ‘So they would both be returning the excess?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 9. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from and Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn abu Nasr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ibrahim, Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who made an al-Rahn (security deposit and mortgage) deal which is for one hundred dirham with a value of three hundred dirham and it was consumed; if he had to pay two hundred dirham to the other party. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, because he has taken al-Rahn (security deposit) in which there is increase and loss.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if half is consumed?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is proportionate.’ I then asked, ‘Do they return to each other the extra?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, that it true.’”
